A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Pinco work. Their main texts, appendices, equations, tables, and figures are readable and support matching retained, relocated, and newly added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons, component ablations, a 31-participant user study, and appendix convergence and qualitative results.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds Flux-Pinco evaluation, expanded ablation results, and special-case experiments in Appendix G.

M1.justification: v1 implements Pinco through subject cross-attention in Hunyuan-DiT. v2 adds an MM-DiT adaptation that concatenates latent and subject keys/values for subject-aware MM-attention (Section 4.1, Equation 3), applied to Flux's double-stream and single-stream blocks. This changes the attention procedure, rather than merely testing the unchanged implementation on another backbone.

E1.justification: The 88K-image training collection, 300-item evaluation collection, and MSCOCO evaluation remain. Appendix G adds limited qualitative coverage of multiple subjects, incomplete foreground objects, conflicting lighting, and an anime-style domain.

E2.justification: Table 1 replaces the SD3 ControlNet comparator with Hunyuan ControlNet, enabling a same-backbone comparison with HY-Pinco. Appendix Figures 17–19 add Hunyuan ControlNet while retaining SD3 ControlNet and Adobe Firefly. The other comparator families and user-study competitors remain.

E3.justification: v2 introduces the Flux-Pinco model configuration and tests transfer of a FLUX.1-dev-trained adapter to an anime-style fine-tune without further training. The main 300 images × 3 prompts × 2 seeds design, 1024×1024 resolution, learning rate, crop ratios, and metric suite remain. Newly explained compositing and LPIPS details do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds robustness investigations of subject-count mismatches, multiple identities, missing object parts, lighting conflicts, and transfer across styles. Table 2 broadens quantitative assessment of the existing component ablations, including a full no-RoPE result row. The earlier attention-map and convergence analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify two random generation seeds per image/prompt and retain the same user-study sample size. Neither adds repeated-training-run information, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds Hunyuan ControlNet and Flux-Pinco results; Flux-Pinco reports OER values of 7.87% and 6.84% and VQAScore 0.918. The renamed HY-Pinco retains v1's numerical results. Table 2 adds metrics for existing ablations, including no-RoPE OER values of 290.44% and 68.64%, and Appendix G adds qualitative findings. These are additional results, not same-setting improvements over v1's Pinco.

T1.justification: Equation 3 newly defines the MM-DiT subject-aware attention operation using concatenated latent and subject keys/values. The diffusion loss and Hunyuan attention remain mathematically equivalent, while Equation 4 formalizes the already described feature fusion. No theorems or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: an efficient plug-and-play DiT adapter with three components that improve foreground preservation and text-aligned background generation. The Flux extension supplies evidence for the previously claimed general applicability.

C2.justification: New Appendix H identifies difficulty preserving slender objects and handling unusual viewpoints. Appendix G discusses completion or occlusion of missing parts, reconciliation of lighting conflicts, and transfer between structurally compatible models. Section 5.2 also frames text-alignment advantages against same-backbone ControlNet comparisons.

D1.justification: v2 documents Flux integration into 19 double-stream and 38 single-stream blocks, foreground compositing, and foreground-region LPIPS evaluation. It omits v1's disclosure of 24 A100 GPUs, batch size 5 per GPU, and an internal refiner. These omissions reduce implementation information but do not establish that the underlying processing stopped.

R1.justification: Citations expand to Flux/Flux-fill, ATA, salient-object-aware background generation, and additional generation, restoration, and safety research. The related-work taxonomy and central positioning against image-prompt adapters and ControlNet-style injection remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 revises introductory and methodological wording, generalizes terminology from subject cross-attention to subject-aware attention, and renames the augmentation subsection. Author information, acknowledgments, and appendix organization also change. The main narrative structure remains, although unresolved citations appear in Appendix B.

P2.justification: v2 adds Flux architecture and special-case figures, revises the framework graphic, and expands or rearranges the main and appendix comparison grids. Table 1 gains backbone grouping, and the two earlier ablation tables become one expanded table. Several existing figures are merely relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for Pinco's claimed portability through an explicit MM-DiT adaptation and comparisons against ControlNet on both Hunyuan and Flux backbones, addressing v1's reliance on a single Pinco backbone. Expanded ablation reporting and the new robustness and limitations sections make effectiveness and applicability more assessable. These gains outweigh the lost hardware, batch-size, and refiner disclosures and unresolved appendix citations.
